---
title: "Reference"
subtitle: "What every template shares, and what each one is free to change."
description: "The contract every carousel template in the gallery obeys: page geometry, the bindings at the top of the file, and the shared helper names."
---

There is no library here.
Each template is a single self-contained Typst file, and copying one gives you everything it needs.

What holds the collection together is the contract on this page.
`tools/lint-templates.sh` checks it, so a template that breaks it does not ship.

## Fixed rules

These protect legibility on a feed, or the reader's ability to act on the deck.
They do not change from one template to the next.

Page geometry
: `21cm × 21cm`, margin `0cm`.
  That is the 1:1 canvas LinkedIn and Bluesky show without cropping.
  Pad inside a slide with `inset:` or `block(width: …)`; never shrink the page.

Slide count
: Six.
  A cover, four content slides, and a closing slide carrying the links.

Type size
: Body text 14 pt or larger.
  A slide has to read at about 250 pixels wide.
  Cover headlines sit between 36 pt and 72 pt.

Colour
: No purple, lavender, violet, fuchsia, or magenta.

Links
: Every visible URL is a clickable `#link()`.
  A bare URL in a PDF is dead text.

Fonts
: Only families vendored in `fonts/`.

## The file skeleton

Every template is laid out in this order, so knowing one is knowing all of them.

```typst
// <family>/<variant>: <one sentence on the visual angle>
// Placeholder subject: Acme Kit 2.1.0. Replace the PROJECT block below.

#set document(title: "Acme Kit 2.1.0", author: "Your Name")
#set text(lang: "en")

// --- PROJECT (replace these) ---
#let project = "Acme Kit"
#let version = "2.1.0"
#let repo-url = "https://github.com/mcanouil/typst-carousel-gallery"
#let date = "2026-01-01"

// --- THEME ---
#let ground = rgb("#…")   // page fill
#let paper = rgb("#…")    // light panel
#let ink = rgb("#…")      // body text
#let muted = rgb("#…")    // secondary text
#let hair = rgb("#…")     // rules and borders
#let accent = rgb("#…")   // the one accent
#let slab = rgb("#…")     // code background
#let slab-fg = rgb("#…")  // code foreground

#let display = "…"
#let body = "…"
#let mono = "…"

#set page(width: 21cm, height: 21cm, margin: 0cm, fill: ground)
#set text(font: body, fill: ink, size: 15.5pt)
#set raw(theme: none)
#show raw: set text(font: mono, ligatures: false)

// --- HELPERS ---

// --- SLIDES ---
```

All sixteen bindings are required, even in a template that leans on only a few.
Someone adapting a deck should find the same names in the same place every time.

## Shared helper names

Where a template implements one of these ideas, it uses this name and this signature.
The body is where the visual identity lives, and it is free.

| Helper | Signature | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `url-link` | `(url)` | A clickable URL that prints as its own address. |
| `kicker` | `(txt, tint: accent)` | The small tracked label above a headline. |
| `chip` | `(txt, tint: accent)` | A boxed word: a status, a tag, a count. |
| `code-slab` | `(body, size: 13pt, tint: accent)` | A code panel. |
| `shot` | `(path, width: 100%)` | A framed screenshot. |
| `footer` | `(n: none, total: 6)` | The rule and the line under it. |
| `slide` | `(n: none, body)` | One page. |

A template needs no helper it does not use, and must not rename one it does.

Two ways of writing `slide()` are both correct:

```typst
#let slide(n: none, body) = page(fill: ground)[…]

#let slide(n: none, body) = {
  block(width: 100%, height: 100%)[…]
  pagebreak(weak: true)
}
```

The contract fixes the signature, not the mechanism.

## Families

A family is a visual system: what a slide is built out of.
A variant is one answer within that system.
Variants of one family share the structure and differ in palette, type, and motif.

| Family | The system |
| --- | --- |
| `editorial` | Paper, a serif, and a single column. |
| `terminal` | Shell chrome and monospace as the leading voice. |
| `technical` | Grids, rules, and measurement marks. |
| `dataviz` | A chart carries the slide. |
| `panels` | Content divided into cards or ruled rows. |
| `control` | A user-interface metaphor: switches, states, crosshairs. |
| `poster` | Display type and one large motif. |
| `screenshot` | Framed product shots as the evidence. |

## The placeholder subject

Every template announces the same fictional release, Acme Kit 2.1.0.

That is deliberate.
Holding the words constant makes the designs comparable, which is the point of a gallery.
`Acme` is a well-understood stand-in, so no reader mistakes it for a real project, and every link points back at this repository so no template ships a dead URL.

## Checking a template

```bash
bash tools/build.sh --png <family>/<variant>
bash tools/lint-templates.sh <family>/<variant>
```

The lint checks the geometry, the bindings, the colours, the links, the fonts, and the catalogue entry.
It cannot check that a slide looks right, so read the six PNGs as well.
